newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest hits highs as region's markets stay flat.
newsitem.headline: Budapest hits highs as region's markets stay flat.

text.p: The Hungarian share market tagged on to Wall Street's bull run this week but other east European markets were mostly flat, while there was no trading at all in Bulgaria.
The Central European Share Index (CESI), which measures price movements in 50 selected Hungarian, Czech and Polish shares, eased 12.9 points.

Developments in Russia have generally had a strong impact on regional markets, but traders said the ousting of Russian security chief Alexander Lebed was unlikely to influence the region's bourses substantially.
BUDAPEST

The Budapest Stock Exchange's BUX index set new record highs every day this week, helped by Wall Street's rise and positive corporate news. By the second half of the week, however, the pace had slowed as the market sought new impetus.
"We have reached a level where no major changes can be expected until fresh news comes out," Robert Agoston of Daewoo Securities said.
"Two major developments can be expected, one is that Moody's and S&P examine Hungary's rating," he said, adding they might upgrade Hungary's rating to an investment grade.
The other will be a new batch of corporate results, to be released later this month, which traders generally expect to be good.
However, on Friday the BUX index fell 21.13 points, although its 3,707.45 point close was up 67.77 points from last Friday.
PRAGUE
The PX50 posted its first gain of the month on Friday as a turnaround in the fortunes of major issues, which began on Thursday, finally translated into upward movement on the index.
Despite Friday's gains, the PX50 lost 1.75 percent over the week to close at 532.9. Traders cautioned against treating one day's trading as evidence of the start of a sustained recovery.
"Some more interest from abroad has been seen but its still taking a long time and for a real wave of buy orders we'll have to wait longer," said Lubomir Vystavel of ING Barings.

Vystavel said that SPT Telecom, which rose 20 crowns to 3,100, attracted the most activity on the bourse on Friday. SPT took 19.3 million crowns worth of the total 33.3 million crowns traded during the continuous trading session.
SPT accounts for more than 20 percent of the PX50's total capitalisation and often has a decisive influence on the direction of the market.
WARSAW
The Warsaw bourse fell this week and analysts saw it extending its losses in a profit-taking downtrend after an 11 percent rise since early September. A possible rebound could emerge later next week.
The WIG index fell 1.4 percent from last Friday's close to 14,718.4 points but analysts said it should not go lower than 14,400 or 14,000.
Some stocks performance next week might be influenced by their earnings reports for September, due after the market's close on Friday.
BRATISLAVA

The Bratislava bourse saw another week of slack trading activity and brokers do not expect the current flat trend to reverse in the near future. The 12-share SAX index eased 0.83 point to end at 202.99 on Friday.

"The market would need an increase of trading activity, which would mean the entry of new foreign investors, but the trading is generally expected to remain flat over the next two weeks," said Jozef Cimra of ING Barings.

"Foreign investors seemed to have testing our market over the past few weeks, but an increase in their trading activity would probably require more stable general economic situation in Slovakia," Cimra said.
BULGARIA
No corporate issues were traded on the Bulgarian stock market this week as investors turned towards repo facilities, pushing repo turnover to an all-time high.
The 13-share Reuter All Bulgaria Stock Index (RABSI) closed at 41.28 points, unchanged from last Friday.
LJUBLJANA

In Ljubljana share prices fell 2.4 percent as the SBI index dropped 31.5 points to 1,268.20. Health resort Terme Catez underperformed the market plummeting 8.9 percent. The biggest gainer, financial consultancy Dadas, soared 11.1 percent.
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks were steady to lower on Friday, despite leading shares closing the week up.
Traders said the market was heading for a correction after rallying for a month as investors became more cautious.
BUCHAREST

Bucharest prices drifted higher on Thursday after three consecutive sessions of falls. Volumes were modest and traders did not expect turnover to rise substantially before new companies join. The bourse said recently that 14 companies had applied for a listing and would soon be traded.

The VAB-Index, an unofficial value-weighted index of all listed stocks computed by Vanguard SA securities, rose 1.2 percent this week to 295.3 points on Thursday, after touching year lows for the previous three sessions.
TIRANA

The Tirana bourse posted the highest weekly volume of transactions in 364-day T-Bills in its five-month history as 440 million leks worth in bills changed hands during this week's two sessions on Monday and Thursday.
